title: Charles Bridge
blurb: Prague’s medieval stone arch bridge over the Vltava, begun in 1357 under Charles IV. Sixteen sandstone arches carry a 516 m deck lined with 30 Baroque statues between three Gothic bridge towers.

systems.name: Deck
systems.description: The 516 m sandstone roadway deck, 10 m wide, with its cobblestone paving.

systems.name: Arches, piers and ice guards
systems.description: Sixteen sandstone arches on massive piers, each pier shielded by an ice guard against floes and floods.

systems.name: Parapets
systems.description: The north and south parapets carrying the continuous alley of statues.

systems.name: Statues
systems.description: Thirty Baroque statues, fifteen per side, erected 1683-1714 and now all replicas.

systems.name: Old Town Bridge Tower
systems.description: The Gothic gateway tower on the Old Town side, a symbolic victory arch on the coronation route.

systems.name: Lesser Town towers
systems.description: The pair of bridge towers on the Lesser Town side, one Gothic and one Romanesque.
